title: League articles of Maximilian I and the Sienese orators, Pisa, November 1496 (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 18, DECODE R4806)

documents.shelfmark: ASSi, Concistoro 2308, fasc. 2 "Lettere in cifra", no. 18 (DECODE R4806)
documents.route: Maximilian I (royal chancery, Pisa) <-> the orators of Siena

transcription.source: Project transcription (agents K and L, 24 Sept 2026, transcripts/no18v.txt) for the project's key; George Lasry's transcription (by Claude, refined by the author in CTTS) for his reading
transcription.notes: Lengths: 1,469 cipher signs per George Lasry's report (181 separator dots, 144 clear stretches); the project's transcription counts 1,456-1,459 tokens. George Lasry says accurate transcription was the main obstacle across the fascicle.

documents.date: November 1496 (undated; fixed by George Lasry from Maximilian I's stay at Pisa, Ziegler's secretaryship and the Valiano fighting)

system.summary: Per George Lasry's key: 60 distinct signs. Homophonic substitution with double-letter signs (rr, pp, ss, ll, cc, tt), dotted or barred signs as nulls and a few code capitals (B = the League, X = the enemy, M.X.). The project's transcription named 30 signs (look-alike glyphs merged) and read it as a simple substitution.
system.notes: Look-alike pairs separated on the image: hooked n = q, plain n = e; o = g, lead-in o = o; open OO = i, closed pair = ll. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from siena1421 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): each letter of the bundle has its own key; this entry is no. 18 only. System fields revised 18 Oct 2026 from George Lasry's key (17 Oct 2026).

prior_solution.where: Not in print or online (Meister 1902, Cecchini 1952, Senatore 2009 checked). George Lasry's independent solution (17 Oct 2026) came after the project's of 24 Sept 2026.

conditions.human_role: Set the goal (decipher the 29 letters; try the 42 filed keys first). Instructed that DECODE records marked Decrypted are to be trusted as read. George Lasry recovered the key independently (17 Oct 2026, with CTTS and Claude) and sent his reading and dating; it was compared here with the project's key.
tools: CTTS (George Lasry, transcription and refinement of his independent solution)
models: Claude (George Lasry's solution, version not stated)

solution.what: Found the whole busta Concistoro 2308 on DECODE (keys R4746-R4789, letters R4790-R4814, R1858), missed by the 23 Sept scan; downloaded 131 images with the project cookie (the session that worked on all the Concistoro letters).
Viewed and indexed the 43 key records of fasc. 1 (R4746-R4789); compared their alphabets by eye with this letter's signs: none fits.
No. 18 transcribed (agent K) and re-verified on the images (agent L: 14 of about 1,450 tokens changed; transcripts/no18v.txt).
No. 18 (1,456 tokens, 211 point-divided Latin cipher words, 30 signs): homsolve2 words=1 with the Latin LM recovers the key unaided (Siena-Empire treaty articles, Ponte a Valiano, Florentines).
Split on 14 Oct 2026 from siena1421 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): each letter of the bundle has its own key; this entry is no. 18 only.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1172 tokens, 32 types, la order 4: reading -2.464 per letter; random keys -5.005 (z 4.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.003 (mean -3.027, z 26.4); annealer on the real text -2.281. Verdict: underdetermined.

George Lasry, with CTTS and Claude, independently of the project: transcription by Claude refined in CTTS; key recovered by Claude from cribs taken from the surrounding clear Latin; all cipher passages read; dated to Pisa, November 1496 (report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026).

George Lasry's key compared sign by sign with the project's (lasry_comparison.md): 35 of his 38 letter and doubled-letter signs carry the same value in ours (3 of them as glyphs our transcription merged with a look-alike), 1 differs (cc vs c), 2 single-occurrence signs are not in ours. His reading fills our unread and doubtful words (10 graded H, 3 M) and replaces our dating (1510s-1520s) with Pisa, November 1496.

Second comparison, made on main from George Lasry's page (merged 20 Oct 2026): the one passage his page prints ('restituerentur, ita tamen quod ipsi Senenses ad requisitionem Florentinorum sint contenti de stando iuri coram Cesare, dummodo Florentini etiam de illis que ipsi occupant sint contenti stare iuri coram ÷') is word for word transcripts/no18_reading.txt L4.24-28 (ours spells 'ocupant'). His key table against ours by shape: every common sign and every look-alike split found here on the images agrees. Its two apparent differences (our d = a, a = i against his i, u) came from the stale solver output keys/no18_key.txt; the final key in no18_reading.txt has d = i and a = u, as lasry_comparison.md records. Dating sources added: Regesta Imperii XIV, Sanudo Diarii I, Ulmann 1884, Pecci 1755.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): this project's transcription (agent K, verified by agent L), George Lasry's decryption and translation (lasry_report.md, verbatim) and, as a separate file, the project's own earlier reading, with the comparison of the two; key = the project's keys/no18_key.txt (Lasry's key figure is docs/siena18_key.png, outside the folder; his CTTS transcription is not in the repository).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.967; polyphony 0.057; 298 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.281

outcome.method_basis: Recovered twice from the ciphertext alone: by this project (homsolve2 with word boundaries and a Latin model, 24 Sept 2026) and independently by George Lasry with Claude from cribs in the surrounding clear Latin of the same document (17 Oct 2026).
outcome.fraction_read_source: George Lasry's full decryption (lasry_report.md): 1,469 cipher signs (his count); unread marks counted in his text: ÷ x4 and ✱ x2, single signs each; one doubtful word s[anctissima]? (counted unread, about 1 sign): 1,462 of 1,469 = 99.5%. The project's own reading: transcripts/no18_reading.txt, 1,271 of 1,459 tokens (87.1%).

texts.label: No. 18 (R4806), treaty articles subscribed by Niccolo Ziegler, [Pisa, November 1496]: George Lasry's reading and this project's independent one
texts.summary: Latin articles negotiated by Sienese orators with Maximilian I's side, subscribed by his secretary Niklas Ziegler, dated by George Lasry to Pisa, November 1496: Siena to ready artillery and lend the King 5,000 ducats repayable in two months, open war near Ponte a Valiano against the Florentines with passage, victuals, 100 men-at-arms and 60 light horse, and have its claims against Florence judged by the Emperor. Two independent ciphertext-only readings: Lasry's complete one (decryption and translation in lasry_report.md, adopted) and this project's of 24 Sept 2026 (transcripts/no18_reading.txt, 87.1%), compared in lasry_comparison.md.
